subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Conversion and Error Detection (W11 B1)

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'She writes a letter every day.'

options.option_text: A letter is written by her every day.
A letter was written by her every day.
A letter has been written by her every day.
A letter is being written by her every day.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: 'She WRITES' (Simple Present). Passive: 'is/are + past participle'. 'A letter IS WRITTEN by her every day.' Rules: (1) Object becomes subject; (2) Subject becomes 'by + object'; (3) Verb form: is/am/are + V3. Trap: 'was written' = Simple Past passive (wrong tense); 'has been written' = Present Perfect passive; 'is being written' = Present Continuous passive.

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'The police arrested the thief yesterday.'

options.option_text: The thief was arrested by the police yesterday.
The thief is arrested by the police yesterday.
The thief has been arrested by the police yesterday.
The thief was being arrested by the police yesterday.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: 'arrested' (Simple Past). Passive: 'was/were + past participle'. 'The thief WAS ARRESTED by the police yesterday.' The time adverb 'yesterday' is retained. Trap: 'is arrested' = Simple Present passive (wrong tense for a completed past action); 'has been arrested' = Present Perfect passive (cannot be used with 'yesterday' — specific past time marker); 'was being arrested' = Past Continuous passive (implies the action was ongoing, not completed).

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'They are constructing a new hospital in the city.'

options.option_text: A new hospital is constructed in the city by them.
A new hospital is being constructed in the city by them.
A new hospital has been constructed in the city by them.
A new hospital was being constructed in the city by them.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active: 'are constructing' (Present Continuous). Passive: 'is/are being + past participle'. 'A new hospital IS BEING CONSTRUCTED in the city by them.' Pattern: am/is/are being + V3 = Present Continuous Passive. Trap: 'is constructed' = Simple Present passive (wrong tense — loses the 'ongoing' aspect); 'has been constructed' = Present Perfect passive (completed action — wrong); 'was being constructed' = Past Continuous passive (wrong tense).

questions.stem:
Convert to Active Voice:
'The book has been read by all the students.'

options.option_text: All the students read the book.
All the students are reading the book.
All the students have read the book.
All the students had read the book.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Passive: 'has been read' = Present Perfect Passive. Active: 'have + past participle' = Present Perfect Active. 'All the students HAVE READ the book.' Conversion: passive subject ('the book') becomes object; passive agent ('by all the students') becomes subject. Trap: 'read' (Simple Present) — loses the perfect aspect; 'are reading' = Present Continuous (completely wrong tense); 'had read' = Past Perfect (wrong tense — 'has been' maps to 'have', not 'had').

questions.stem:
Identify the correct Passive Voice of:
'Who teaches you English?'

options.option_text: By whom are you taught English?
By whom were you taught English?
By whom English is taught to you?
Who is you taught English by?

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active: 'Who teaches you English?' (Simple Present interrogative). Passive: 'By whom are you taught English?' Steps: (1) 'Who' → 'By whom' (object pronoun with preposition); (2) 'teaches' → 'are taught' (Simple Present Passive); (3) Question word order: By whom + are + subject + past participle. Trap: 'were you taught' = Past tense (wrong tense); 'By whom English is taught to you' = statement order (wrong for a question); 'Who is you taught' = wrong pronoun case and wrong word order.

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'Nobody has informed me about the meeting.'

options.option_text: I had not been informed about the meeting by nobody.
I have not been informed about the meeting.
I was not informed about the meeting.
I have not been informed about the meeting by nobody.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active: 'Nobody has informed me' (Present Perfect with negative subject). Passive: 'I HAVE NOT BEEN INFORMED about the meeting.' When the subject is 'nobody/no one', the passive omits 'by nobody' (redundant double negative). The negation is captured by 'not been'. 'By + nobody' creates a double negative and is wrong. Trap: 'had not been' = Past Perfect (wrong tense); 'was not informed' = Simple Past Passive (wrong tense — loses present perfect aspect); 'by nobody' = double negative (incorrect).

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'Please close the door.'

options.option_text: The door should be closed.
The door is closed please.
Let the door be closed.
The door has been closed.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Imperative sentences in passive: 'Let + object + be + past participle.' 'Please close the door' → 'LET THE DOOR BE CLOSED.' The 'please' is dropped in the passive transformation. Trap: 'should be closed' implies obligation/suggestion (adds meaning not in original); 'is closed please' = grammatically awkward (passive of simple present, not imperative); 'has been closed' = Present Perfect passive (completed action — wrong meaning).

questions.stem:
Convert to Active Voice:
'The match will be won by our team.'

options.option_text: Our team won the match.
Our team has won the match.
Our team wins the match.
Our team will win the match.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Passive: 'will be won' = Future Simple Passive. Active: 'will + base verb'. 'Our team WILL WIN the match.' The agent 'by our team' becomes the subject. Conversion: will be + V3 (passive) → will + V1 (active). Trap: 'won' = Simple Past Active (wrong tense — 'will be' maps to future, not past); 'has won' = Present Perfect Active (wrong); 'wins' = Simple Present Active (wrong).

questions.stem:
Identify the ERROR in the passive construction:
'The letter was wrote by him last night.'

options.option_text: 'was' should be 'is'
'wrote' should be 'written'
'by him' should be 'by he'
No error

questions.explanation: B is correct. The error is 'wrote' — in passive voice, the verb must be in the past participle (V3) form, not the simple past (V2). The past participle of 'write' is 'WRITTEN', not 'wrote'. Correct: 'The letter was WRITTEN by him last night.' Trap: 'was' is correct for Simple Past passive; 'by him' is correct (objective pronoun 'him' after 'by', not 'he').

questions.stem:
Convert to Passive Voice:
'They will have finished the project by Monday.'

options.option_text: The project will be finished by Monday.
The project will have been finished by Monday.
The project has been finished by Monday.
The project had been finished by Monday.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active: 'will have finished' = Future Perfect Active. Passive: 'will have been + past participle' = Future Perfect Passive. 'The project WILL HAVE BEEN FINISHED by Monday.' The agent ('by them') is omitted as it adds no meaningful information. Pattern: will have + V3 (active) → will have been + V3 (passive). Trap: 'will be finished' = Future Simple Passive (loses the 'completed before a future time' meaning); 'has been finished' = Present Perfect Passive (wrong tense); 'had been finished' = Past Perfect Passive (wrong tense).
